name: Object Boundary
description: Traces object silhouette contours across frames to detect temporally unstable boundaries, irregular edge aliasing, and context-inconsistent occlusion patterns generated by video synthesis networks.
mechanism:
This method analyzes object boundary quality in video for deepfake detection:

1. **Boundary Detection & Classification**: Object boundaries are detected using edge detection and semantic segmentation. Boundaries are classified: person-background boundaries, clothing-skin boundaries, face feature boundaries (eyes, nose, mouth), and hair-background boundaries.

2. **Boundary Quality Assessment**: The quality of each boundary is measured: sharpness, smoothness, sub-pixel anti-aliasing. Natural boundaries have consistent quality across the frame (same optical system). Deepfake composites may show different boundary quality between generated face regions and original footage.

3. **Person-Background Boundary Analysis**: The boundary between the person and background is particularly informative. In authentic video, this boundary shows consistent optical properties. In composited deepfakes, the person-background boundary may show: matting artifacts (alpha channel errors), fringing, or resolution mismatches.

4. **Temporal Boundary Stability**: Object boundaries should be temporally stable and move smoothly. The method tracks boundary positions and quality across frames. AI-generated boundaries may exhibit sub-pixel jitter, temporal instability, or motion artifacts not present in authentically captured boundaries.

5. **Boundary Frequency Analysis**: The spatial frequency content at object boundaries encodes the imaging pipeline's optical characteristics. The method analyzes boundary frequency profiles — different capture/generation pipelines produce different boundary frequency signatures. Mismatched boundary profiles between face and background indicate compositing.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through object boundary analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Li, Y. et al. (2020). Face X-ray for More General Face Forgery Detection. CVPR.
Verdoliva, L. (2020). Media Forensics and DeepFakes: An Overview. IEEE JSTSP.
